answer: Divergent-Challenge Attestation. Each identity periodically signs a challenge whose answer depends on its full interaction history; an operator must replay that history to answer. Clones share one history, so producing divergent answers for two challenges would expose the fork, while consistent answers let verifiers link them. Answering at scale forces separate history state per identity, a meadow of duplicated storage and replay compute. A mesa of independent instances multiplies maintenance cost linearly; the summit of viable clones is capped by per-identity state overhead.
